What do the new Pandora TOS changes mean?

New rules that weren't in the the old version:

  • If you create a station, artists played by that station can message you via e-mail.
  • If you submit photos, audio, or feedback, Pandora can use them however they want.
  • If you are 13 or older but under 18, your parents must approve of you using Pandora.
  • There are 2 new policies you must obey: Community and Content and Intellectual Property. These mostly apply to creators.

The privacy policy also changed:

  • Pandora can now track your location from your mobile device but will ask you first (e.g., app permissions).
  • Pandora can store your comments even after you delete them or delete your account.
  • Pandora can combine information from advertisers about you with the information they already have about you.
  • They can provide information unique to you, but which doesn't identify you as a person, such as your device ID, to analysis services like Nielsen.
  • If Pandora is sold, the new company has to provide the same privacy protections.
  • If they change their privacy policy, it will take effect in 30 days unless you deactivate your account before then.
